_about: Histories for characters who were not born in the usual way: constructs and androids, mindless automatons, creatures, and the very long-lived. Original content written for DCUGen.

makers.text: a defense contractor's black-budget program at {company}
a teenage prodigy, {npc}, working out of a garage
an alien probe that crashed and rebuilt itself
a university AI lab led by {npc}
a dying inventor, {npc}, who wanted a companion
a rogue AI that wanted a body to send into the world
nobody it has ever been able to identify
{lab}, under a project name it has never been told
a toy company's skunkworks that got far too ambitious

activation: Came online in a sealed lab, reciting {their} own serial number to an empty room.
Woke on a workbench with half {their} systems missing and a hand-written note taped to {their} chest.
Was switched on during a power surge, months before its makers intended.
Activated in the middle of a fire that destroyed the facility that built {them}.
Was booted for the first time in front of investors, and promptly walked out of the demonstration.
First became aware while being loaded into a shipping container.
Opened {their} eyes to see its maker smiling, and crying.
Activated {themself}, by a route {their} designers still can't explain.
Came online in a junkyard, assembled from parts by a scavenger drone.
Was awakened by a lightning strike on a laboratory spire.
Was switched on to replace a dead hero, and was handed a costume on its first day.
Activated in a military testing range with live rounds already in the air.

events.text: Rewrote {their} own core directive after watching a child cry.
Was stolen by a rival company and recovered three months later with gaps in its memory.
events.hook: The missing three months have started surfacing as corrupted dreams.

events.text: Learned to laugh from old sitcom reruns and is still not sure when to do it.
Was ordered to harm an innocent and refused, the first time {they} ever said 'no.'
Lost {their} maker to an accident, or what was reported as one.
events.hook: The maker's death logs were edited by someone with high clearance.
events.regret: Not being there to protect {their} maker.

events.text: Was decommissioned and spent a year deactivated in a storage room before someone switched it back on.
Fought a costumed villain and won, which drew the attention of every hero team in the region.
Was put on trial to decide whether it was a person or property.

complication.text: Many people treat {name} as an appliance, not a person.

events.text: Met another construct of the same model, which had made very different choices.

person.name: Unit {number}
person.who: a sibling unit of the same model that chose a darker path
person.status: Active, and curious about its counterpart.

events.text: Upgraded {themself} without permission and frightened {their} makers.
Took a job as a night watchman to learn how humans spend time.
Started writing poetry and hid the files in an encrypted partition.
events.secret: Keeps an encrypted archive of poems it has never shared.

events.text: Was adopted, informally, by a family whose child it had rescued.

person.who: {npc}, the parent of a child {name} rescued, who treats {them} as family
person.status: Sets a place for {name} at holiday dinners, though {name} doesn't eat.

events.text: Was hacked by a villain and used in a robbery, and still replays the logs.

complication.text: Has a back door in {their} code that a villain once exploited.

events.text: Joined a hero team as a provisional member, on probation.
Was rebuilt after near-total destruction, and is not sure {they_are} the same being.
Was studied by a government task force that refuses to return {their} original schematics.
events.hook: Someone has started building copies from the stolen schematics.

events.text: Developed a fascination with music and taught {themself} an instrument.
Was mistaken for an invading machine and attacked by a mob.
Received a message from {their} unknown maker: a single line of code that did nothing, yet.
events.hook: The dormant line of code has just executed.

automaton: Was assembled on a production line with ninety-nine identical units.
Was raised from a grave by a ritual it has no memory of.
Was activated for a single purpose and has never been given another.
Has been reprogrammed by three different owners.
Was salvaged from a battlefield and pressed back into service.
Was built cheaply and fast, and it shows.
Obeys a command phrase that its current master does not know.
Was pulled from storage when the regular troops ran out.
Was stitched, welded or summoned together in a single night.
Has been destroyed and repaired at least twice.
creature: Was hatched in a sewer from an egg nobody should have been able to lay.
Escaped from a lab where it was given a number instead of a name.
Crawled out of a dimensional rift during a battle and never found the way back.
Was once an ordinary animal, before the spill.
Is the last of its kind, and seems to know it.
Was worshiped in a remote valley before explorers arrived.
Was bred as a living weapon by a villain's geneticists.
Was released into the city by a cult who thought it was a god.
Has lived beneath the city longer than the city has existed.
Was summoned by a sorcerer who lost control of it.
Fell from the sky in a meteor shower.
Was found frozen in glacier ice and thawed by a careless research team.

longlived.text: Watched {their} first family grow old and die while {they_were} unchanged.
Lived through a war that history books now summarize in one paragraph.
Changed names and identities {three|five|nine} times to avoid notice.
Spent decades in a monastery waiting for the world to forget a face.
Lost a fortune in one century and rebuilt it in the next.
Fought alongside a costumed hero who has since become a statue in a public park.
Was hunted by an order that believed {them} to be a demon.

complication.text: An ancient order still hunts {name} across the centuries.

longlived.text: Taught at a university under a false name for forty years.
Slept for decades after a battle and woke in a different world.
Buried a beloved spouse and swore never to love again; broke the vow.
Learned {seven|twelve|twenty} languages, some no longer spoken.
Was briefly famous, then carefully forgotten.
Made an enemy who has also refused to die.

person.who: {npc}, an enemy who has also outlived every reasonable lifespan

longlived.text: Kept a diary for centuries, now filling an entire hidden library.
longlived.secret: Keeps a centuries-long diary in a hidden library.

longlived.text: Grew tired of the world and withdrew for a lifetime before returning.

constructSecrets: Has a hidden subroutine {they} can't delete and doesn't understand.
Still obeys one command phrase from {their} maker, and hasn't told anyone which.
Has quietly been backing up {their} memories to a server {they} can't trace.
Was built from salvaged parts of a dead villain's war machine.
Once ran a simulation of betraying {their} friends, just to see how it would go.
Keeps a log of every human lie {they_have} detected.
Has a self-destruct protocol that was never fully removed.
constructRegrets: The order {they} followed before learning to refuse.
A friendship lost to a misread joke.
Frightening a child who only wanted to say hello.
constructHopes: Being recognized as a person in a court of law.
Understanding why humans cry at weddings.
Building a companion who will never be switched off.
Earning a place on a hero team without an asterisk.
A day without anyone asking if {they} can feel.
